title: Redwood migration demo - OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood

Agreed to run a pilot benchmark and share parity spreadsheet and security pack.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Michael Ortiz (LumenAI CTO), Sara Kim (ML Eng), Jon Peters (Platform Eng), Olivia Zhang (Security)

Summary (auto): demo focused on migration parity and operational considerations for switching from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're super excited to walk through how Redwood can map to your existing OpenAI/Anthropic/Together setup. Quick intros?
[00:08] Michael (LumenAI - CTO): Hey Ava, Michael here, Sara and Jon and Olivia are on. We're mainly evaluating parity — we have a lot of production traffic on OpenAI and some Anthropic models.
[00:15] Sara (ML Eng): yep, hi. we use a mix of chat completions and embeddings. some function calling; lots of short requests but a long-tail of bigger prompts.
[00:22] Ava: great. i'll hand over to Daniel to show the API parity and then we'll demo the console and Optimize recommendations.
[00:27] Daniel (Redwood SE): cool, thanks. so first slide — apologies for the screen share hiccup — but the practical approach is mapping endpoints and parameters. for example, OpenAI's chat/completions temperature/top_p/stop maps 1:1 to Redwood's generate endpoint. function calling is supported but with slightly different param names in the SDK — we have examples.
[00:45] [00:45] Daniel: note on streaming: we support server-sent events and websocket style streaming similar to OpenAI. There are small differences in chunking when using continuous batching, you'll see in perf.
[01:02] Jon (Platform Eng): how about tokens and tokenization? we rely on OpenAI token counts for billing and analytics.
[01:07] Daniel: great q. our Console shows token-level breakdowns and tokenization aligns with common tokenizers; we'll share a parity table because token counts can vary by a few percent between models. we also surface per-route cost so you can compare unit economics vs your current spend.
[01:22] Olivia (Security): SOC2? SSO? KMS? we need to know if we can meet our compliance requirements.
[01:27] Priya (Redwood): yes — VPC/private deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. we'll send the SOC 2 + security pack. for private on-prem we can also provide air-gapped options.
[01:38] Michael: nice. specifically, do you provide customer-managed KMS for key rotation?
[01:42] Ava: yes, customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations; for private we can support HSM requests too.
[01:47] [01:47] Daniel: jumping back to parity — for Anthropic, you might be using their 'claude-instant' style calls. we map those to our lower-latency rw-instant variant; quality tuning and top_k/top_p equivalents are in the mapping doc. some of the naming in autogenerated transcriptions is weird — you might see "claude" spelled funny in notes, sorry.
[02:10] Sara: function calling — we rely on structured outputs for some agents. how close is Redwood's function call behavior?
[02:16] Daniel: we support structured outputs and tool calling; the difference is our SDK returns the tool payload slightly differently (payload vs arguments object). we showed a sample snippet in the deck. almost identical flows, just small code adaptions.
[02:29] [02:29] Michael: ok, about latency — we have a sub-100ms p95 SLO for short prompts. how achievable is that on hosted vs dedicated?
[02:36] Daniel: for short prompts p95 under 100ms we recommend Dedicated with pinned capacity and optimized kernels. Hosted can hit low-latency in many regions but dedicated gives predictability. also Optimize can suggest batching thresholds and quant profiles to lower cost while meeting latency.
[02:52] Jon: what about continuous batching — our traffic pattern is spiky.
[02:56] Priya: continuous batching and autoscaling policies let you handle spikes and optimize unit cost; you can set burst capacity and routing policies — e.g., route critical traffic to dedicated, fallback to hosted.
[03:08] [03:08] Daniel: quick demo — i'm opening the Console. top-left you see models and per-model perf; here's a canary rollout page, you can compare A/B across model versions, token cost delta, and a trace view.
[03:22] [03:22] Daniel (sharing screen): so here's an example where we mapped your openai/gpt-4o->rw-4o (example mapping), we kept parameter compatibility: messages array, role tokens, system messages intact. the embed endpoint supports same input->vector shape, slight diff on returns (we return vector as vector field).
[03:40] Sara: will this break our existing client code?
[03:43] Daniel: minimal changes — we provide drop-in SDKs and a compatibility table. for the rare cases you use edge-cases (OpenAI specific behaviors), we list code snippets to adapt.
[03:51] [03:51] Michael: safety and moderation — we currently use OpenAI moderation endpoint. do you provide something similar?
[03:56] Ava: yes we have built-in moderation policies and hooks to integrate third-party classifiers. we can also forward to your existing classifiers in pipeline. the Console surfaces flagged content and you can tune thresholds.
[04:08] Olivia: audit logs retention? we need 7 years for a small subset of projects.
[04:12] Priya: we have configurable retention; for Private deployments you can control logs and retention in your own S3 or on-prem store. we'll include that detail in the security pack.
[04:22] [04:22] Daniel: switching to Optimize — this is our tool that analyzes traffic and recommends batching windows, cache prefixes, and quantization levels. here's an example: their chat traffic suggested 8x batching for 512-token tails and a quant profile (4-bit) for lower cost with <2% quality loss.
[04:40] Sara: can you do per-route quantization? some routes can tolerate lower quality.
[04:43] Daniel: yes, per-route and per-model profiles. Console will show expected quality regression and cost savings.
[04:50] [04:50] Michael: about embeddings — we use them heavily for vector search. any parity gotchas?
[04:54] Daniel: embeddings are straightforward; we support OpenAI-compatible shapes and we supply a versioned model catalog. you might see slight float differences and vector norms; we'll include a comparison for your test corpus. also we provide bulk import tools to migrate existing embedding indices if needed.
[05:10] Jon: networking — for Private, what's the path? VPC peering vs private link?
[05:14] Priya: we support VPC peering and private link options depending on your cloud provider. for on-prem we do VPN/IPSec.
[05:20] [05:20] Michael: ok good. let's talk about a pilot. we want to validate: (1) cost parity (2) latency SLOs (3) function-calling parity (4) security.
[05:29] Ava: perfect. recommended pilot: we provision a trial org, load your sample prompts and traffic simulator, run A/B benchmarks across hosted vs dedicated and across model variants, then Optimize produces suggested profiles.
[05:40] Daniel: we'll run a 50k token synthetic run and a production-sampled run. expected deliverables: latency percentiles, token cost per-route, and fidelity comparison on a prompt set.
[05:51] Sara: one more question — are there any differences in prompt templating or system message handling? we rely heavily on system message priming.
[05:58] Daniel: same semantics; there are minor differences in stop token handling across some model families — parity table will show exact behavior.
[06:07] [06:07] Michael: any immediate blockers from our side? data residency or legal?
[06:11] Olivia: legal will want to review data processing agreement; also we need a security questionnaire answered.
[06:15] Ava: we'll attach the DPA and an initial security questionnaire; Priya will be primary contact for security follow-up.
[06:21] Priya: noted. I'll also include an architecture doc for private deployment.
[06:25] [06:25] Daniel: closing with an example mapping snippet — show the curl for openai->redwood equivalence (messages array, temperature, max_tokens) and an example for function-calling. i'll add the SDK snippet too.
[06:40] Michael: thanks. seems reasonable. any pricing notes for pilot?
[06:44] Ava: pilot is usually free credits + usage-based for larger benchmarks; we'll include trial pricing and Dedicated commit options in follow-up.
[06:52] [06:52] Olivia: last comment — please include our security contact on the pack.
[06:55] Ava: will do. quick recap of next steps...
[06:58] [06:58] Ava: Recap: send parity spreadsheet, SOC2/security pack, provision trial org, run perf benchmarks, schedule SE deep dive next week. Any final q's?
[07:08] Michael: no, thanks.
[07:10] Ava: great, thanks everyone, we'll follow up on the action items.

End of call.
